senses.gloss:
Anvā-khyāna.--From the literal translation (‘after-story’) the meaning of ‘supplementary narrative’ seems to follow. In two of its three occurrences in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa this sense is hardly felt, the expression being used to indicate a subsequent portion of the book itself. But in the third passage it is distinguished from the itihāsa (‘story’) proper, and there must mean ‘supplementary narrative.’ Cf. anuvyākhyāna.
Foot notes vi. 5, 2, 22; 6, 4, 7 (the reference is to vi. 6, 4, 8).
xi. 1, 6, 9.
Cf. Sieg, Die Sagenstoffe des ṛgveda, 34.
